> 115	  startRender(opts): RenderJobState {
> 116	    const state: RenderJobState = { id: opts.jobId, status: 'rendering', progress: 0, outputPath: opts.outputPath };

> 118	    (async () => {
> 119	      const fps = fpsToInt(opts.fps);
> 120	      const resolution = opts.outputResolution && VALID_RESOLUTIONS.has(String(opts.outputResolution))

> 123	      // 1) Submit through the billing chokepoint with a real minted User Zero JWT (re-mint once on 401).
> 124	      let res: Response | null = null;
> 125	      for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) {
> 126	        const jwt = await mintUserZeroJwt(attempt > 0);
> 127	        res = await fetch(`${SUPABASE_URL}/functions/v1/video-render`, {
> 128	          method: 'POST',
> 129	          headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${jwt}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
> 130	          body: JSON.stringify({
> 131	            engine: 'hyperframes',
> 132	            topic: `studio:${opts.project.id}`,
> 133	            composition: { mode: 'studio-project', project_dir: opts.project.dir, fps, resolution },
> 134	          }),
> 135	        });
> 136	        if (res.status !== 401) break;
> 137	      }
> 138	      const body = await res!.json().catch(() => ({} as Record<string, unknown>));
> 139	      if (res!.status !== 202) {
> 140	        // Honest surface (PT-BR reaches the studio UI). 503 = billing gate OFF (Fila Sovereign) — no charge happened.
> 141	        state.status = 'failed';
> 142	        state.error = String((body as { detail?: string; error?: string }).detail ?? (body as { error?: string }).error ?? `video-render HTTP ${res!.status}`);
> 143	        return;
> 144	      }
> 145	      const renderId = String((body as { render_id?: string }).render_id ?? '');
> 146	      state.stage = `submetido (render ${renderId.slice(0, 8)})`;
> 147	      state.progress = 0.1;
> 148	
> 149	      // 2) Observe the ledger row until the worker (video-bridge, native FR-VS-050 engine) finishes.
> 150	      const t0 = Date.now();
> 151	      while (Date.now() - t0 < RENDER_TIMEOUT_MS) {
> 152	        await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, RENDER_POLL_MS));
> 153	        const { data: row } = await admin.from('video_renders').select('state, user_id').eq('id', renderId).maybeSingle();
> 154	        if (!row) continue;
> 155	        if (row.state === 'running') { state.progress = Math.min(0.8, state.progress + 0.1); state.stage = 'renderizando (nativo)'; continue; }
> 156	        if (row.state === 'failed') { state.status = 'failed'; state.error = 'Render falhou no worker — mcoCoins reembolsados (finalize_video_render).'; return; }
> 157	        if (row.state === 'done') {
> 158	          // 3) Materialize the bucket MP4 at the path the studio routes serve.
> 159	          const key = `${row.user_id}/${renderId}.mp4`;
> 160	          const { data: blob, error: dlErr } = await admin.storage.from('video-studio-assets').download(key);
> 161	          if (dlErr || !blob) { state.status = 'failed'; state.error = `Render concluído mas o download do bucket falhou: ${dlErr?.message ?? 'vazio'}`; return; }
> 162	          writeFileSync(opts.outputPath, Buffer.from(await blob.arrayBuffer()));
> 163	          state.progress = 1;
> 164	          state.status = 'complete';
> 165	          state.stage = 'concluído';
> 166	          return;
> 167	        }
> 168	      }
> 169	      state.status = 'failed';
> 170	      state.error = 'Timeout de 15min aguardando o worker — a linha video_renders segue viva (reaper re-claima).';
> 171	    })().catch((e) => {
> 172	      state.status = 'failed';
> 173	      state.error = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
> 174	    });

> 176	    return state;
> 177	  },

- **The bucket is genuinely default-deny.** `20260701120000` inserts a private bucket with no policies. I confirmed there is no blanket `USING (true)` policy on `storage.objects` — every existing policy is scoped by `bucket_id = '<other-bucket>'`. So anon/authenticated get zero grants on `video-studio-projects`; only the service role (RLS-bypass) can read or write it. The migration comment's default-deny claim is accurate.

- **No lower-privileged path can inject attacker-controlled keys.** The only service-role writer to this bucket is `sweepProjects` (sync.ts:48), which builds keys as `projects/${id}/${rel}` where `id` passes `SAFE_ID` and `rel` comes from `walkDir(dir)`. `walkDir` uses `readdirSync` (never yields `.`/`..`), and the studio's file-mutating routes (`rename`/`copy`/`write` at studio-server dist:2075-2118) are all jailed through `resolveWithinProject`→`isSafePath`, which canonicalizes with `realpathSync` and rejects any path escaping the project dir (including symlink escape). So a loopback user behind the SSO vhost cannot create a file whose name contains a `../` segment inside a project dir, meaning no such segment can ever reach a bucket key. `generate-carousel` accepts an arbitrary `out_bucket` but is service-role-gated (Bearer `SB_SECRET_KEY`) and its only caller (`reshape-pillar`) hardcodes `generated-images` — no user path targets this bucket.

- **Consequently** the `join(staging, rel)` in `materializeProject` (sync.ts:97) has no reachable traversal: `rel` is derived only from keys the constrained sweep itself wrote. The missing explicit `..`-sanitization on `rel` is a defense-in-depth gap, not an exploitable vulnerability, given the private default-deny bucket + service-role-only writer + single-tenant trusted-infra context. That falls under the excluded hardening-only category.

Other surfaces checked and cleared:
- `server.ts` change is only `startSyncLoop` wiring + SIGTERM/SIGINT flush; the static `GET *` route and its `resolve(UI_DIST, '.' + rel)` jail are unchanged.
- `adapter.resolveProject` remains double-guarded (`SAFE_ID` + `startsWith` jail) before the async materialize; the 60s negative cache is DoS-adjacent only (excluded).
- The atomic `renameSync(staging, dir)` with staging/`dir` both under the fixed root and `id` SAFE_ID-constrained introduces no path escape; concurrent-materialize interference is a race (excluded) with no security impact.
- `smoke-studio-sync.ts` is test-only (excluded).

One forward-looking note (not a current finding, just flagging for when the migration's "user_id prefix slots in when multi-tenant lands" happens): once multiple tenants share this bucket, `materializeProject`'s unsanitized `rel` and the service-role-wide `sweepProjects`/`listRecursive` would need per-tenant key-prefix enforcement and `..`-rejection on `rel` before download. Worth adding the `rel` traversal guard defensively at that point.
